vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: zworker
Version: 1.0.2

The 'zworker' skill bundle is designed to interface with a local Electron-based automation application via a REST API on localhost:18803. The included Python scripts (e.g., zworker_api.py, sync_users.py, run_task.py) facilitate task management, schedule control, and synchronization of OpenClaw user identifiers to the local service. No evidence of data exfiltration to external domains, unauthorized file access, or malicious prompt injection was found; all functionalities align with the stated purpose of local task automation.

llm.summary: The skill appears to be a legitimate local controller for a zworker app, but there are multiple inconsistencies between the documented runtime instructions and the provided scripts (how user data is obtained, paging conventions, and minor API parameter names) that should be clarified before trusting it.

dimensions.detail: Name/description (control local zworker via localhost:18803) matches the code: all network calls target http://localhost:18803 and the scripts perform the declared operations (list/run tasks, manage schedules, sync users, fetch notifications). However, the SKILL.md claims the skill will read OpenClaw's openclaw.json channels field to assemble users for syncing; the provided sync_users.py does NOT read openclaw.json and instead expects data from stdin, --users, or --file. This is a meaningful mismatch between claimed capability and actual implementation.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md instructs the agent to read OpenClaw runtime data (openclaw.json / cli / gateway) and to use an OpenClaw message tool to send messages; the scripts assume those inputs are provided externally (stdin/args) and do not implement direct reading of OpenClaw config or any message-sending implementation. There are also inconsistent paging conventions: SKILL.md/refs say pageNumber starts at 1, but the Python API uses page_number default 0. These gaps mean following the SKILL.md literally may fail or cause the agent to attempt to read files/paths that the scripts won't use.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: Instruction-only with Python scripts included; no install spec, no remote downloads, and all network requests are to localhost. Uses requests if available or urllib as fallback. This is low install risk.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill requests no environment variables, no external credentials, and interacts only with a local HTTP service. That is proportionate to its stated purpose. There are no hidden credential accesses in the code.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always is false and the skill is user-invocable; it does not try to persist itself or modify other skills. Autonomous invocation is allowed (platform default) but not combined with other privilege escalations here.

dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance:
This skill is intended to control a local zworker application and makes only localhost HTTP calls, which is appropriate for that purpose — but before installing or enabling it, note these issues:

- Inconsistency: SKILL.md says the agent will read openclaw.json to gather channel/userid info, yet sync_users.py requires the user list via stdin/--users/--file. Confirm how the agent will obtain the user list in your environment (and update the skill or provide the file/input if needed).
- Paging and API minor mismatches: the docs treat pageNumber as 1-based while the scripts use 0-based page numbers; setCronId parameter name in docs ('cronId') differs from code ('id'). These can cause off-by-one or parameter errors when invoking endpoints.
- The skill can trigger tasks and (un)enable schedules on a local service — ensure the zworker instance on localhost:18803 is trusted and secured, since the skill will call endpoints that perform actions.
- There is no message-sending implementation in the code; the skill expects an external 'message' tool/environment to deliver notifications. Verify how your agent will send messages (and that sending targets are correct) before enabling notification-related features.

Recommendations: review and (if needed) patch the skill so its runtime behavior matches SKILL.md (or update SKILL.md to match the scripts), test the scripts locally against your zworker instance, and ensure the local zworker is trusted and not exposed to untrusted networks. If you need higher assurance, ask the publisher to clarify the openclaw.json handling and paging conventions.
